note: ERA 21. H8 (A101, Q118): a developed lot costs the city money to serve. Every income term in this project was decoration because income ran FOUR TIMES expenses at every size and every difficulty - a steady 25-year city took 20,268 a month and spent 5,048 - and the reason was that a developed lot paid tax and cost nothing, while the only expenses were the civic buildings and a penny a road tile. economy.serviceCostPerLevel is what a lot costs per level per tile; per-TILE upkeep was tried twice and rejected twice (era 0, era 1) because it bankrupts a young town without touching a rich one, and this scales with what the city has GROWN instead. Measured as a four-rung ladder over eight cities a difficulty: at 0 the treasuries are 6,466k relaxed / 5,021k steady / 2,534k demanding; at 6/12/22/35 they are 5,837k / 4,264k / 1,258k with nobody dead; at 12/25/45/70 DEMANDING COLLAPSES from 1,644 residents to 163 with one city of eight dead. The useful range of this lever is bounded by demanding's own margin rather than by the mechanism - it pays 120% of every expense and keeps 80% of every tax, so it has nothing to absorb a new one with - J4 (A106) re-cuts it. The eight-seed ladder said 6/12/22/35 killed nobody and the 200-game SWEEP said nine demanding cities of two hundred reached a hundred residents and ended empty - never tune on five seeds, from the other direction - so the rung came down again: at 3/6/11/18, measured over FORTY demanding cities, the dead count is 0, the population is 1,618 against 1,632 and the treasury 1,955k against 2,374k. A first step, deliberately small, and the reason it is small is demanding's own margin - J4 (A106) re-cuts it and raises this. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era21.md. ERA 20. H6 (A100, Q134): ground too steep to build on is not zoned. S11 let a junction's height move within six metres of its own land and took hilly 128 from 177 cliffs on the walked route to 30; what was left was 20 m corridors with 10 m of land between their ends, which no cutting a person would dig fixes at 15%. Kjell took the expensive option: the city is not on the cliff in the first place. development.maxZoneSlope is 6 elevation steps, which IS the street's own limit - road.maxGrade 15% of a 20 m tile is 3 m is six half-metre steps - so you may not zone ground a street could not be built on. It is canZone's rule, so it is the reducer's: one rule, the same for a player and for the deputy, answered with RESULT.TOO_STEEP rather than 'that cannot go there'. The deputy skips steep tiles when it zones, because a zoning run is a transaction and one steep tile would refuse the whole strip. Measured on three 64 maps a style, 25 years: hilly goes from population 1,015 with 505 zoned tiles to 1,872 with 334 - nearly TWICE the city, because the zoning that goes down is zoning that can be reached and served instead of scattered up a hillside - and rolling is unmoved (1,837 to 1,734 population, 301 to 293 buildings, inside three-seed noise). Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era20.md. ERA 19. H5 (A96, Q130): the deputy repairs a grid a disaster cut in two. G2 made every carrier RUN reach a live piece of grid and left the other half open - the deputy connects a building when it BUILDS it and never looks again, so a component that loses its producer stays dark for the rest of the game, and what repair there was came incidentally from new buildings' carriers. Measured by cutting every wire in one column of a 15-year city: seed 1003 darkened 84 buildings of 234 and had 54 still dark a year later; seed 404 darkened 80 and had six still dark after FIVE years. With the rule: 0 and 5 after one year, and the grid back to one component on 1003. Two defects in the first cut, both the same shape as G2's: it ran carriers out of the COAL PLANT two hundred and forty times, because a producer on an under-capacity component is itself unlit and a plant's darkness is keepSupplied's problem rather than a route to find; and it counted a turn as spent whether or not the run laid anything, so the deputy stopped doing everything else and the city it was repairing went from 84 dark to 211. connectToNetwork now reports whether it actually laid a run. Only when the city HAS the capacity: a brown-out is a shortfall to build out of, not a grid to re-stitch. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era19.md. ERA 18. H4 (A97, Q131): the deputy dezones what it paves. It crosses its own zoned land on purpose - B9 measured that refusing to cross a zoned strip cut the sweep's population by half, because crossing one is how blocks join - and since era 15 a lot cannot grow on a road, so those tiles were zoning that had been paid for and could never be used: 591 of 1,688 on seed 1003, 639 of 1,646 on an eight-seed mean, two in five. Every path that lays road dezones under it, not only buildBlock: the rail station's access road and the ferry terminal's are connectToNetwork runs, and leaving them out left exactly ONE zoned-and-paved tile a city, which is the kind of remainder that reads as a rounding error and is a missed caller. The dead runCarrier() goes in the same commit - no caller anywhere, superseded by connectToNetwork's search, and it called apply() directly rather than issue(), so it would not have counted its own refusals. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era18.md. ERA 17. H3 (A99, Q133/Q111): the mayor plants parks and builds police stations. The deputy has built neither for the life of the project - 0 parks and 0 police stations in a 25-year city - so every balance number this project has ever published was measured on a city that had no park to carry G3's landValueBonus and no patrol to answer B3b's crime. One rule each, both in the shape the fire station has had since B1a: a police station per deputy.buildingsPerPolice (40, mirroring the fire station exactly - same footprint, same price, same upkeep) and a park per deputy.buildingsPerPark (20, the cheapest thing in the catalogue at 60 and 2 a month). Both use (n + 1) * per <= others rather than n * per < others, which is the form T7 got wrong twice and which fires at a town of ONE building; the fire station keeps its older form deliberately, because a town wants a fire service from the first house. Measured in three arms over eight seeds, 25 years: base 1,582 population, land value 125.3, crime 1.6, 219 buildings; parks alone 1,973 / 132.4 / 1.9 / 261; police alone 1,826 / 126.1 / 2.0 / 253; both 2,082 / 135.5 / 0.8 / 305. Each rule grows the city on its own and together they take crime to half what it was - a park reaches crime through land value (A93's path) and a patrol reaches it directly. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era17.md. ERA 16. G3 (A88, A91, Q119/Q123/Q127): landValueBonus becomes a rule and the last two dead catalogue fields are deleted. The field has been on the park since the catalogue was written and landValuePass never read it, so a park reached the ground beside it only through its negative pollution and (since era 10) the leisure coverage layer. It is now deposited over def.radius with coverage's own falloff - 100 per cent at the building, nothing at the radius - by amenityValue() in civic.js, and a RUINED building deposits nothing, because a fire must not improve the neighbourhood. The city hall gains landValueBonus 16 over radius 8 (A91), so six thousand and two hundred a month buys something besides a quest. storage (a water tower that stores nothing: supplyPass allocates per month with no carry-over) and capacity (what a civic building's lit-window fraction would be a share of, which client/world/ may not read - ruling 032) are deleted from the data and the mirror, which leaves UNREAD_FIELDS EMPTY for the first time in the project. The sweep can barely see this rule and that is the honest reading: the deputy builds exactly three bonus carriers a city (one railStation, one marina, one ferryTerminal) and never a park, which is Q133. The MECHANISM is measured beside it, in the same scripted town over 40 seeds with and without parks: before, a park moved land value 63.8 to 97.1 and crime not at all; after, 63.8 to 118.5 with crime 13.3 to 6.7 and population 74 to 86. Crime falls because crimePass reads land value, which is A93's ratified consequence arriving on schedule. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era16.md. ERA 15. G1 (A85, Q116): a network refuses a building, and a grown lot refuses a street. placeNetwork has refused a building on the rail layer alone since A66 (clearOfBuildings on one spec line); road, wire and pipe have been laid straight across one since slice 1.3, which let a player bury their own park under a road and let the deputy's wire cross a coal plant. The rule is now in placeNetwork for every kind, checked before ownership so the answer is needsBulldoze - what to do about it - rather than a permission code. The refusal alone broke the deputy: 169.9 refusals a city on an eight-seed mean and not one avenue, because the avenue is an UPGRADE of the busiest street and that street had houses standing on it. lotFree - placeBuilding's counterpart for a lot nobody placed - never read the road layer, so a block of zoning painted across a street grew lots on the carriageway: 90.9 of 295 buildings a city, for the life of the project. Both halves are one act, measured in three arms: base 90.9 lots on a street and 8.0 avenue tiles; the refusal alone 74.3 and 7.3 with 170 refusals; both 0.0 and 10.0 with none. The price is the third of every city that was illegal - 295 buildings to 238 and population 2,269 to 1,758 on the eight-seed mean. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era15.md. ERA 14. G2 (A86, Q117): the deputy's carriers reach a LIVE grid, for every building it builds rather than for the rail station alone, and it will not put a building where no carrier can arrive. Three defects, each found by the seed the others hid: connectToNetwork joined the NEAREST carrier tile, which is usually a dead stub the deputy laid earlier (seed 404 ended with 228 of 439 buildings holding a pipe and no water while the city held 2,240 capacity against 997 demand); the search started at a lot's top-left tile, which for a 2x2 has two of its own tiles as neighbours, so seed 1003's fire station was sealed in by its own footprint and the run issued nothing and said nothing; and findSpotFor would put a clinic inside a solid block of buildings, which no run can ever reach (seed 404, twice). A spot now needs a side a carrier could ARRIVE at - reachable from the grid, not merely empty, which is the weaker version of the same mistake that seed 1111 showed - and a run that reaches nothing counts itself in deputy.unconnected, because a silent failure is how this lived for the project's life. Over twelve seeds the power grid went from eight components to one and the dark buildings from 60 a city to 0. More carrier is laid for it (1,476 wire tiles to 1,739 on an eight-seed mean), which the city pays for. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era14.md. ERA 13. Q128 (A94): decayOneIn is 3, symmetric with growthOneIn. Era 12 implemented the roll with the 6 that was sitting in the file and nobody had ever chosen either number - decline had been three times faster than growth, and era 12 made it 2.7 times SLOWER (a cut-off lot took eight years to die, against three years to grow through all four levels). At 3 a lot dies in four years and the two forces mirror each other. The lever was measured first: an eight-seed ladder over decayOneIn 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 gave a clean monotone churn column (1,949 / 798 / 492 / 362 / 173 abandonments in 25 years) and a population column that was pure noise at that sample size, which is the project rule about five seeds arriving on schedule. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era13.md. ERA 12. G4 (A92, Q124): decay ROLLS like growth. development.decayOneIn has been in this file since the development pass was written and was read by nothing, so a lot above the growth threshold grew one month in growthOneIn while a lot below the decay threshold lost condition every time it was scored - decline three times as fast as growth, which nobody chose. development.roadWeight and development.crowdingWeight are deleted in the same breath: scoreLot has no such terms and a number nothing reads is a promise rather than a rule. Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era12.md. ERA 11. T7 (A70): five cheap rows - clinic, policeHQ, fireHQ, reservoir, wasteFacility - and five deputy considerations, which is why this is an era rather than a catalogue edit. The clinic is the only health a young town can afford and the deputy builds one per deputy.buildingsPerClinic; the headquarters are one-offs past headquartersAtPopulation; the reservoir replaces the pump past reservoirAtPopulation; the tip is built once the city is tipAtPopulation big AND its pollution over developed land passes tipAtPollution (5, which is what the sweep actually reports - the first cut guessed 24 and only ever fired in a village, where two power stations and nine houses is a filthy city by that measure, and it bankrupted every town it fired in: seed 1003 peaked at SIXTY people against 1,260 without it). Measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era11.md. ERA 10. T6 (A67, A70): leisure and education are coverage layers of their own - tiles.leisure and tiles.education, hashed and saved - fed by five new definitions (plaza, library, stadium, school, university) plus the park and the marina, with a funding row each. They reach the city twice: civic.amenityValueDivisor adds them to land value beside the three departments, and civic.amenityDemand puts the average over DEVELOPED land into the residential pool. The deputy builds a school every deputy.buildingsPerSchool buildings and a plaza every buildingsPerPlaza, so a headless city has both - without that every sweep in the project would have measured a town that reads zero on two of the five layers. Re-measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era10.md. ERA 9. P87 re-mixed the deputy's OWN stream - Math.imul(seat, 0x9e3779b1) ^ index where era 8 had (seat << 20) + index - inside a review round that changed no rule, and nobody re-ran the sweep. Every deputy decision in every city moved with it, so era 8's report describes a set of worlds that no longer exists: measured at 60 games a side, relaxed's median population went 2275 to 2477, steady's 2415 to 2318, and one steady city died. Re-measured with tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era9.md. No rule changed; every number moved because the worlds did, which is exactly what era 8 said about itself. T5a arrived in the same commit and is not in it: gate.air and airport.maxDrop are ERA 0, UNTUNED and reach nothing a deputy builds - proved by 60 games a side with and without T5a coming back byte-identical. Numbers from era 8 are void, not roughly comparable. ERA 8. Q113: the deputy draws from its OWN stream, a pure function of the seed, the tick, the seat and the draw's index within the turn, instead of from state.rng - which development, fire and disasters also draw from. One extra deputy action used to shift when every later fire started and every later building grew, so a sweep comparing two eras compared two worlds rather than two rules. No rule changed; every number below moved because the worlds did. ERA 7. T4 (A67, A68): water bodies are derived - a flood over the water layer giving each body a size and whether it reaches a map edge - and three buildings hang off them. A marina needs harbour.marinaMinBody tiles of one body beside it. A ferryTerminal and a freightPort are SEA gates: buildable anywhere a marina is, and LIVE only where the body reaches an edge, which is what gate.sea's terms, its fare and its commuter sink follow. The deputy builds a marina and a terminal past deputy.harbourAtPopulation. ERA 6. T2 (A65, A66, A79): rail is a network of its own, a railStation is a GATE, and worldgen places rock and marsh. A live gate - a station whose line reaches a map edge, powered and with road access - adds gate.rail's integer terms to the regional demand pool, seeds the commuter field as a sink and takes gate.rail.farePerResident from every resident within gate.rail.range. build.rail and upkeep.rail are the line's. ERA 5. T1a (A60): a second road kind. An avenue carries traffic.avenueCapacity times a road before it reads as full, and the commuter field crosses it at traffic.avenueStep against a road traffic.roadStep - so a grid with one avenue routes onto it. build.avenue is its price. ERA 4. B1a (A62): a fire nobody fights spreads and burns slowly rather than dying with the house it started in (fire.unfoughtPercent, unfoughtSpread, unfoughtDamage), and the deputy builds a fire station per deputy.buildingsPerStation buildings - until now it built none, and no gate city in the project has ever had a fire service. Era 3: B9 (A81): the deputy lays a road only within deputy.roadReach tiles of a lot that is built, or zoned and supplied, so a played town grows outward and has an edge; see reports/balance-era3.md. Era 2 is left to T1/T2's re-pin (A79). Otherwise unchanged from era 1 — ERA 1. Tuned 2026-08-29 against tools/sim_sweep.mjs over 200 games per configuration; see reports/balance-era1.md. Changed from era 0: civic.pollutionAverage now averages over developed land instead of the whole region, so it reads 9 instead of 0 and can drive something. RE-TESTED AND REJECTED, for the second time: per-tile wire and pipe upkeep. At 1 each it put p25 treasury on 0 and cut p25 population from 647 to 187 — it bankrupts weak cities without touching the rich ones, which is what the era-0 note already said. ACCEPTED, not fixed: runaway treasuries, median 1.9M and p95 3.8M after 25 years. Numbers from era 0 are void, not roughly comparable.

gate._comment: T2 (A65): the Outside is gate buildings, not a second simulation. A LIVE gate adds these integer terms to the regional demand pool, seeds the commuter field as a sink, and takes a fare from every resident within range. ERA 0, UNTUNED against the bases in `demand` below (400/150/150).

air._comment: T5 (A69): the largest terms there are, plus a LANDING FEE - a flat monthly sum a live airport earns from the aircraft rather than from the residents near it, which is why an airport in an empty region is still worth something. ERA 0, UNTUNED.

airport._comment: T5 (A69). maxDrop is the largest difference in `tiles.elevation` the airport's footprint may contain - a runway is flat, and the engine has no metres. Six units is three metres at the renderer's half-metre relief step, a tenth of the grade a road is allowed over the same 120 m, because a road climbs and a runway does not. On a rolling map about one 6x4 site in ten qualifies; on a hilly one almost none, which is the intent.

harbour._comment: T4 (A67, A68). marinaMinBody is how many tiles of one body a marina needs beside it - a pond is not a harbour. `water` next to this is the UTILITY's, and a second block of that name silently replaced it. ERA 0, UNTUNED.

development._slope: H6 (A100): the steepest step in elevation units between a tile and a four-neighbour that may still be zoned. Six, because that is the grade a STREET may climb: road.maxGrade is 15%, a tile is 20 m and an elevation step is 0.5 m, so 15% of 20 m is 3 m is six steps. You may not zone ground a street could not be built on. Measured over three 128 maps a style: it leaves rolling at 100% of its buildable tiles (93% are at 4 or less) and flat at 100%, and takes hilly from 100% to 41% - which is the point, and is still 17,000 tiles of city.

economy._service: H8 (A101, Q118): what a developed lot costs the city to SERVE, per level. Until era 21 a lot was pure income - it paid tax and cost nothing - while the only expenses were the civic buildings and a penny a road tile, so a steady 25-year city took 20,268 a month and spent 5,048, banked the rest for twenty-five years and ended on 4.7 million. Per-TILE upkeep was tried twice and rejected twice because it bankrupts a young town without touching a rich one; this scales with what the city HAS GROWN rather than with what it has paved, so a village of nine level-1 cottages pays 225 a month and a city of 160 lots pays seven thousand. The ladder is steep on purpose - a level-4 tower is four cottages' worth of water, refuse and road - and it is calibrated from the lot census of a 25-year steady city (45/29/13/8 residential by level, 17/7/1 commercial, 29/9/2 industrial) and it is chosen from a four-rung ladder measured over eight cities a difficulty: at 0 the treasuries are 6,466k relaxed / 5,021k steady / 2,534k demanding; at 6/12/22/35 they are 5,837k / 4,264k / 1,258k with nobody dead; at 12/25/45/70 DEMANDING COLLAPSES, from 1,644 residents to 163 with a city dead of eight. The useful range of this lever is bounded by demanding's margin, not by the mechanism - it pays 120% of every expense and keeps 80% of every tax, so it has nothing to absorb a new one with. The eight-seed ladder said 6/12/22/35 killed nobody and the 200-game SWEEP said nine demanding cities of two hundred reached a hundred residents and ended empty - never tune on five seeds, from the other direction - so the rung came down again: at 3/6/11/18, measured over FORTY demanding cities, the dead count is 0, the population is 1,618 against 1,632 and the treasury 1,955k against 2,374k. A first step, deliberately small, and the reason it is small is demanding's own margin - J4 (A106) re-cuts it and raises this.

fire._unfought: B1a (A62): a fire is unaddressed when at least unfoughtPercent of the building's own fire risk is left after coverage - no station in range - and it then spreads unfoughtSpread times as readily while consuming its house more slowly, so it outlives what it is standing on and reaches the next one.

disasters._comment: era 0, untuned. Frequency is difficulty.disasterOneIn, which already existed; this is only the shape of one.

traffic._comment: era 0, untuned. roadCapacity is load units per tile before a street reads as full.

deputy._comment: A81 (B9): the deputy lays a road only within roadReach tiles of a lot that is built, or zoned and supplied; expand reaches a little further than the doctrines that hold back. Era 3. T2: railAtPopulation is the size at which it lays a line to the edge and puts a station on it - just above avenueAtPopulation, so the order is the main road first and the railway after it.
